name: save-load-visual
description: Visual verification of the save/load UI: multiple save slots, auto-save indicator, save/load buttons, export/import options, slot metadata display (date, level, cash, playtime), and IndexedDB backend for web persistence.

expect.note: confirmed via direct trace: cash stays flat with no employees/buildings/vehicles to drain it

steps.description: Answered through the event dialog's own buttons (EventModal). clickIfPresent, not clickSelector: this step follows a bare tick, so whether an event fired is a random roll and the dialog may not be on screen at all -- the console command it replaced no-ops in exactly that case. When a dialog IS up, a real click has to work, and the usability gate is the same one clickSelector uses, so an inert control still counts as unclickable. Second click dismisses the outcome panel the choice opens.

When a dialog IS up, a real click has to work, and the usability gate is the same one clickSelector uses, so an inert control still counts as unclickable. Second click dismisses the outcome panel the choice opens.

Left unmarked: "quicksave" isn't a real UI slot -- SavesModal.ts only exposes 'auto' and numbered 'slot_N' (SAVE_SLOT_COUNT) slots. The real UI flow is demonstrated for real below (steps 10/11/16, clicking #bs-saveload-btn and a numbered slot), just under a different slot name than this console-only quicksave.
Open the Save/Load panel (multiple slots, auto-save row, export/import, slot metadata) via its top-bar button.

SavesModal.ts's saveToSlot() re-renders the slot list but never calls hide() (unlike loadFromSlot(), which does) -- the modal stays open after a save and its .bs-confirm-overlay tier covers the toolbar underneath, blocking the next step's click. Closes it explicitly via the header's close button.

expect.note: the real UI slot_1 here goes through SavesModal.ts's own IndexedDB-backed persistence -- a completely separate backend from the console save/load commands' in-memory quickSaveSlots map used above. This is the actual save the later load step reads back.

steps.command: drill_plan grid rows:2 cols:2 spacing:3 depth:6 start:15,15
steps.description: Drill a small plan after slot 1 was saved, so the blast below craters terrain the saved slot does not know about. depth corrected from 4 to 6 (Ground rule #15/Finding #42's class, the whole-suite audit before Phase 3): this step never clicks the grid tool's depth stepper (data-field="depth"), so the real drag always produces the panel's own 6m default regardless of what's declared. This file's own expect blocks only assert hole/charge/sequence counts around the affected blast (depth-insensitive), so this is a metadata-only correction -- verified both modes still pass unchanged.
Blast a crater into the live scene after slot 1's save, so the load step below must actually regenerate terrain (not just leave the cratered grid on screen) to prove itself.

Load back slot 1 by clicking the Saves modal's own Load button (SavesModal.ts, main.ts's setOnLoad handler) — not a raw console command — so this step exercises the click-driven path that must regenerate the grid, replacing the post-blast crater above with clean terrain matching the saved state. The command field stays the inert `state` read (rather than `load slot:...`) so command mode does not pre-clear the crater itself and mask a regression in the click path.

expect.note: command mode's own command field is the inert `state` read (see this step's description) -- it never actually reverts anything, so these values hold here simply because the post-blast state already matches them (blast always zeroes hole/charge/sequence counts, and nothing in this file ever spends cash). In a real browser, the same values hold for the opposite reason: the click genuinely reverts to slot_1's pre-blast save. Both paths converge on the same scalars, but only interaction mode is actually testing the load -- the terrain/voxel revert this step's whole point is about has no state field to check at all, only the screenshot.
